title: Widower's Wood - An Iron Kingdoms Adventure Board Game - Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wzSn1b5XXtk

Daniel (@dungeondive) reviews Widower's Wood, the Iron Kingdoms adventure board game and prettier sibling to The Undercity — a game he'd long avoided for its looks before caving and being pleasantly surprised. It's less a dungeon crawl than a co-op tactical skirmish built on tight positioning: movement and range max out around two squares, so heroes jockey for spots almost like chess against amphibious bog trogs. Monsters spawn by dice roll, with a colour system (red/blue reserves, purple bosses) deciding which type appears and villain cards driving a simple but unpredictable enemy AI. The heroes are the draw — each genuinely distinct, wielding feat-card decks that boost dice, trigger reactions, and let allies strike on the enemy's turn, plus ability decks unlocked with experience. Daniel's main caution: complexity creeps in through keyword rules buried on a glossary page rather than the main rulebook, making solo play a bookkeeping chore — this is a two-player game at heart. Replayability is limited (a seven-chapter campaign) and it's pricey for the content, but the components are high quality and the tactical decision-making has real meat. He recommends it over The Undercity for its colour and character.

----

Have you ever bought a game you'd been avoiding purely on looks, only to be won over? And do you draw the line where hidden keyword rules make a game too fiddly for solo play?
